title: No claude in the cloud, including review and closeout
description:
OPERATOR CONSTRAINT, 2026-09-22: 'everything OFF claude in the cloud.'

The rest of xte takes the IMPLEMENT role off claude. This tick takes the other two. [roles.review] and [roles.closeout] are both kind = claude, model = opus, and a cloud run reaching wave 4 would start a claude process in the container on exactly the path this epic exists to close.

WHAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN AN EDIT, established 2026-09-22: role routing is SUBSTRATE-BLIND today. Config.Resolve(role, tier) in internal/runconfig/resolve.go takes a role and a tier and nothing else; [orchestration] substrate decides WHO ORCHESTRATES, never which model a role gets. And the container reads the target repo's own .tick/runners.toml, so cloud and local read one file. Change [roles.review] in place and local review loses opus too.

That is not obviously wanted. The config's own comment calls review 'the frontier-tier review at epic completion' and says opus 'is not available in pi at all'. A frontier review of a diff locally is a different judgement from what a cloud container can run, and collapsing them loses something real.

So: make role resolution substrate-aware, so the cloud can be fully off claude while a local run keeps its frontier review. Shape is open and is part of the work - a per-substrate overlay on [roles.*] is the obvious one, and it should look like the [roles.*.tiers.*] overlay that already exists rather than a second unrelated mechanism.

THE FAILURE THIS MUST NOT HAVE: a cloud run that silently falls back to a claude role because no cloud overlay was declared for it. Absent cloud routing for a role is a REFUSAL at run start, naming the role, not a default. hn0 reached claude by inheriting a default nobody chose, and this tick is downstream of that lesson.
notes:
2026-09-22 15:37 - WHY THE SPLIT IS THE POINT, AND NOT AN OVER-ENGINEERING (operator, 2026-09-22).

'local is ok on claude (uses my max subscription)'.

So this is economics, not principle. A local claude run bills against the operator's Max
subscription and is free at the margin. A cloud run bills per token against the factory's
own credentials. That is the entire reason cloud and local should resolve [roles.review]
and [roles.closeout] differently, and it is why collapsing them - taking opus out of
.tick/runners.toml altogether - would be the wrong fix even though it is the one-line one.

Anyone implementing this who finds substrate-aware resolution awkward and is tempted to
just delete the claude roles: don't. The frontier-tier review at epic completion is wanted
locally and is affordable there. It is unaffordable and unavailable in a container, where
pi cannot run opus at all.
